name: Credential Management (password and federated)
plain: Lets a site store and fetch saved passwords through the browser.
meaning: Gets a stored username and password after the person picks an account, without scraping form fields.

access.prompt_ui: Account chooser sheet; auto sign in option
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Lets a site store and fetch saved passwords through the browser.

limits.headline: Can fetch a saved login after you pick an account in a browser sheet
limits.user_action: You tap the username box or Sign in and choose an account from the sheet
can: Show saved accounts for that site in a chooser
Receive the username and password for the account you pick
Sign you in again next time if you turned on auto sign in
cannot: See saved logins for other sites
Get a password without the chooser, unless you allowed auto sign in
Work in Firefox or Safari; those use built in autofill instead
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge support it. Firefox and Safari do not.

story.what_it_is: Lets a site save and fetch your login through the browser.

marketing.name: Credential Management API
marketing.pitch: Describes a way for sites to ask the browser to create, store and retrieve credentials such as passwords and federated logins.

story.for_you: You may see a small chooser listing your saved accounts, or you may be signed in with no typing at all. After sign up the browser may ask to save your login.
story.for_makers: Makers get smoother sign in without reading form fields by hand. Auto sign in lifts returning visitor rates, which matters for shops, media and games that need the person logged in.

use_cases.example: A returning player opens a browser game and is signed in automatically, so the lobby loads with their name and stats.
A shop's single page checkout grabs the saved account so the order goes through in one tap.
A news site signs a subscriber in on page load so the paywall never blocks them.
A web email or notes app restores a signed in account after the browser restarts.
A site ends auto sign in when it sees a risk signal, such as a new device, and asks for a stronger check.
A product team measures how many returning visitors signed in automatically versus manually.

risks: Auto sign in on shared computers
